lesson: When the trip goes off script (B1 · Aula demo · grátis)

cards.definition: To solve a problem or put a situation right.
cards.example:
- The agent sorted out a new seat for me in about four minutes.
A atendente resolveu um assento novo para mim em uns quatro minutos.
cards.note: Separável: com pronome ele abre — sort it out, nunca sort out it.

cards.translation: ficar sem (acabar o estoque de algo)
cards.definition: To have no more of something because it finished.
cards.example:
- The hotel had run out of double rooms, so they gave us a suite.
O hotel tinha ficado sem quartos de casal, então nos deram uma suíte.
cards.note: O que acabou vem depois do of. Sem o of, quem acaba é você: my visa ran out.

cards.translation: com mais passagens vendidas do que assentos
cards.definition: With more tickets sold than there are seats.
cards.example:
- The flight was overbooked and they asked for volunteers at the gate.
O voo estava com overbooking e pediram voluntários no portão.
cards.note: É adjetivo e anda com be. Overbooking é o substantivo que o português adotou.

cards.definition: Money given back to you when something did not happen.
cards.example:
- I asked for a refund, not a voucher, and I asked twice.
Pedi reembolso, não voucher, e pedi duas vezes.
cards.note: Substantivo com força no RÍ. Como verbo, a força muda: they refunded me.

cards.translation: escala longa, com tempo de sair
cards.definition: A long stop between flights, with time to leave the airport.
cards.example:
- I had a six-hour stopover in Madrid, so I left the airport and walked.
Eu tinha uma escala de seis horas em Madri, então saí do aeroporto e fui andando.
cards.note: Escala curta, só trocar de avião, é layover. Stopover é a que vira passeio.

cards.translation: se virar, dar conta com pouco
cards.definition: To manage with the little you have.
cards.example:
- I got by with about fifty words of Spanish and a lot of pointing.
Me virei com umas cinquenta palavras de espanhol e muito gesto.
cards.note: Get by with o que você tem, get by on quanto você ganha. Não é get out.

cards.translation: Tem como…? / Existe alguma chance de…?
cards.definition: A polite way of asking for something difficult.
cards.example:
- Is there any chance you could put me on the earlier flight?
Tem como você me colocar no voo mais cedo?
cards.note: Pede muito e não soa exigente. Depois vem you could + verbo, nunca to.

cards.translation: Isso não me serve. / Assim não resolve
cards.definition: A firm but polite way of refusing an offer.
cards.example:
- A voucher doesn't work for me — I have to be in Porto tonight.
Voucher não me serve — eu preciso estar no Porto hoje à noite.
cards.note: Recusa firme sem grosseria. Diga logo em seguida o que VOCÊ precisa, ou vira só reclamação.

cards.translation: morador, quem é da cidade — substantivo, quase sempre no plural
cards.definition: A person who lives in the place you are visiting.
cards.example:
- The locals eat at ten at night, and no guidebook tells you that.
Os moradores jantam às dez da noite, e nenhum guia te conta isso.
cards.note: Em português é lugar; lugar em inglês é place.

cards.definition: Extremely beautiful, refined or of very high quality.
cards.example:
- The dessert was exquisite — I went back the next night just for it.
A sobremesa estava primorosa — voltei na noite seguinte só por causa dela.
cards.note: Soa como esquisito e é o oposto: esquisito é strange.

exercise.title: When the trip goes off script (B1 · Aula demo · grátis)

questions.explanation: Separable: with a pronoun it must split.

questions.prompt: The hotel had _____ double rooms, so they gave us a suite.
questions.explanation: “Run out OF” + the thing that finished.

questions.prompt: They sold more tickets than seats. The flight was…
questions.explanation: The adjective is “overbooked”; “overbooking” is the noun Portuguese borrowed.

questions.prompt: I asked _____ a refund, not a voucher.
questions.explanation: “Ask FOR” a refund — Portuguese “pedir reembolso” has no preposition.

questions.prompt: I had a six-hour _____ in Madrid, so I left the airport.
questions.explanation: A short one, just changing planes, is a “layover”.

questions.prompt: I got by _____ fifty words of Spanish and a lot of pointing.
questions.explanation: “Get by WITH” what you have, “get by ON” what you earn.

questions.prompt: Tem como você me colocar no voo mais cedo?
questions.answer: Is there any chance you could put me on the earlier flight?|Is there any chance you could put me on the earlier one?

questions.prompt: A voucher _____ — I have to be in Porto tonight.
questions.explanation: Refuse firmly, then say what you do need.

questions.prompt: You want dinner advice from someone who lives there. You ask a…
questions.explanation: In English a “local” is a person. The Portuguese “local” (place) is “place”.

questions.prompt: The dessert was outstanding. It was…
